_meta.scale: All weights are in units of the spec's primary stat (1.00 = one point of it).
_meta.formula: score = ( SUM(stat_value * weight) + dps * dpsWeight + procPoints ) * armorClass[itemArmourType]
_meta.armorNote: Armour class is a per-spec MULTIPLIER on the final score, never a filter, so a big enough stat upgrade still wins -- which is what lets Holy take cloth. See the armorClass table on each spec. This was documented long before it was implemented; until it was wired in, Hunter and Rogue tier 3 outranked Paladin tier 2.
_meta.noLevelScaling: There is NO level scaling on any weight. An earlier version multiplied rating stats by 70/playerLevel on the grounds that a rating point buys more percent at low level. True, but the relative value of a primary stat point rises even faster down there, so scaling only the ratings left them badly overvalued below 60 -- it valued 5 spell crit rating at roughly 4 Strength for a level 13 Retribution paladin, against a real figure near 0.25.
_meta.procNote: Proc value is added in the same points currency by procs.py: damage -> dps -> x dpsWeight; stat buff -> stat x uptime x that stat's weight; mitigation -> effective HP -> x stamina weight / 10. Every scenario constant is named at the top of that file and is an estimate, not sim output.
_meta.level60Note: At exactly level 60 the picks come from Wowhead's Classic BiS guides, not from these weights. A TBC-only item may displace a guide entry only by beating the guide's own top pick by 20%. These weights therefore do not determine level 60.
_meta.hunterNote: Hunters carry TWO weapon weights. dpsWeightRanged 23.8 (in Agility) is derived: 1 Agi = 1 RAP = 1/14 Auto Shot dps, and 1 ranged weapon dps = 1.0 Auto Shot dps x ~1.7 for TBC Steady Shot also scaling off weapon damage. Melee dpsWeight is 0.0 from level 10: the melee weapon is a stat stick whose damage is never dealt. levelling_1_9 keeps a real melee weight because a hunter under 10 does swing it. Hunters cannot wear plate or use maces or shields.
_meta.druidNote: Druids are the first class where weapon DAMAGE is worth zero. In Cat and Bear form the weapon's dps is not used at all; attack power in form comes from the feralAp stat ('+N attack power in Cat, Bear, Dire Bear and Moonkin forms only', 72 items) which is weighted identically to plain ap because in form it IS plain ap. Balance and Restoration never swing either. dpsWeight is 0.0 for all four specs; only levelling_1_9 keeps a real one, because Bear form is not learned until 10. Leather and cloth only -- no mail, plate or shields -- and Staff/Mace/Dagger/Fist/Polearm only: no swords, no axes, no ranged weapon. The Ranged slot holds an Idol.
_meta.roleNote: haste/crit/hit are the MELEE and ranged ratings; spellHaste/spellCrit/spellHit are different stats and neither substitutes for the other. A pure caster spec (paladin holy, druid balance, druid restoration) therefore carries ZERO melee offence -- ap, rap, feralAp, crit, hit, haste, expertise, armorPen, wpnDmg, wpnSkill, str -- and a pure physical spec (warrior arms/fury, all hunter, druid bear/feral) carries ZERO spell offence. Small defensive weights (agi, dodge, parry, block) stay, because they are real. Hybrid tanks (paladin protection, warrior protection) legitimately keep both: they swing AND their threat abilities scale with spell power. check_roles.py enforces this.
_meta.shamanNote: Dual Wield is an ENHANCEMENT TALENT for shamans, not a class skill: elemental and restoration can never hold a weapon in the off hand at any level, and enhancement not before 30. Enhancement dpsWeight 18.0 is derived (1 Agi = 1 AP = 1/14 white dps plus crit ~= 0.089; 1 weapon dps = 1.0 x ~1.6 for Windfury and Stormstrike both scaling off weapon damage) and is the least certain of the three weapon derivations. Elemental and Restoration carry NO armour-class preference because their guide BiS lists are largely cloth. Axe/Mace/Staff/Dagger/Fist only -- no swords, no polearms. Ranged slot holds a Totem.
